title: Bubble.io Pricing in 2026: Plans and Real Costs
summary: Bubble.io pricing ranges from $29 to $549 monthly by tier. See how workload units impact your actual costs and which plan suits your needs.
body_markdown:
## Moving Backend Jobs Out of Bubble With Activepieces


To take background jobs off Bubble's workload meter you can use Activepieces, an MIT-licensed automation tool with 770+ integrations that runs scheduled flows and connects services, but it can't replace the app itself.


It has no page editor or user-facing interface, so it only helps with work that never needed to run inside Bubble.


### What stays in Bubble and what moves


Running on a timer or a poll, not because a user clicked something, is the one trait the jobs that suit moving out share. Each can call Bubble through its Data API to read or write only the records it needs:


- Scheduled syncs that copy records between Bubble and another system
- Nightly data imports from spreadsheets or exports
- Third-party API polling that checks an outside service for changes
- Email digests assembled from Bubble data and sent on a schedule


Each of these, run as a backend workflow, burns workload whether or not anyone is using the app. On Activepieces the run is the meter: 1 credit, however many steps sit inside it.


Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module, so on those a ten-step sync costs ten times the two-step workaround it replaced.


Here the looping, filtering and formatting can be split into small, reliable steps without the bill noticing, and Bubble only handles the reads and writes.


Everything tied to the user's session stays put: pages, logins, privacy rules, the booking form and any workflow that must respond instantly to a click. Splitting those across two tools adds latency and a second place to debug.


Calling into Bubble still costs workload, so the saving comes from the logic that no longer runs inside it, not from the call disappearing.


So the fit is narrow. It pays off when your estimate shows scheduled jobs making up a large share of monthly workload, and it does little when most of the load comes from users browsing and booking.


### How do other platforms price similar jobs


As of 28 October 2026,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) prices a job by its own usage terms, listed on its[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , not in Bubble's workload units. So the Bubble workload figure doesn't carry across.


Count the monthly runs of each moved job, find what the page counts as a unit, and price that number.


Run that count next to your Bubble estimate: a nightly sync is 30 credits a month and a poll every 15 minutes is 2,880, against 1,000 credits on the Free plan and 10,000 on Plus at $20 a month, with $0.007 a credit beyond that.


If the moved jobs cost less there than the workload they free up in Bubble, the split is worth the extra moving part.
